subject: MAP: Performance benchmarking & quantization regression plan — next steps and close timeline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Lee <sandra@enterpriseai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft: Performance benchmarking plan (latency/throughput/TTFT + quant)

Sandra — attaching an initial MAP draft (MAP_EnterpriseAI_v1.pdf) and a proposed performance test plan so we can lock timelines and owners. Key points summarized below; see attached for the full action plan.

Goal: validate performance and quality tradeoffs for the production routes you plan to put behind Redwood by June, and include quantitative pass/fail in the MAP so procurement and engineering have clear close criteria.

Test matrix & metrics (high level):
- Models / variants: baseline FP16/BF16; INT8; INT4 (where feasible)
- Hardware matrix: node-A (v100-scale), node-B (a100), private-customer GPU pool
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95 latency (ms), throughput (tokens/sec), TTFT (time-to-first-token), maximum sustained concurrency, memory consumption, CPU/GPU utilization
- Quality/regression checks: eval harness (prompt set + reference outputs) with metrics (exact-match, Rouge-L, hallucination rate). Acceptance criteria: no >2% drop exact-match for INT8; no >5% for INT4 unless compensated by >2x cost improvement and business sign-off

Schedule & owners:
- Week 1 (Apr 13-17): baseline runs (FP16/BF16) + kernel profile capture — owner: Monica (SE)
- Week 2 (Apr 15-21): INT8 runs + regression evals — owner: Ops/SE
- Week 3 (Apr 20-24): Canary rollout plan & monitoring hooks; procurement/Docs for amended SLA — owner: Karthik / Procurement contact

Deliverables to include in MAP: benchmark CSVs, kernel profile tarball, regression report, canary rollback plan, proposed close date and conditions.

Ask: please confirm priority metrics (we called out TTFT and p95 by default) and the suggested close window (Canary start Apr 20 — full rollout May 4). If that looks good I will finalize the MAP PDF and route the DocuSign for the updated SLA terms.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_EnterpriseAI_v1.pdf (PDF)]

Karthik — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side:
- Prioritize TTFT and p95 latency for user-facing endpoints (we want p95 < 200ms ideally).
- INT8 is interesting; INT4 is attractive on cost but we need stronger evidence on quality degradation risk before we'll sign off.
- Procurement: please send the updated SLA draft and a DocuSign link when ready.

Can you include a short canary rollback decision tree in the MAP (thresholds we can agree on)? Otherwise the schedule looks fine. Looping James in Procurement to track SLA docs.

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sandra Lee <sandra@enterpriseai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Performance benchmarking plan — baseline + quant runs (preliminary results)

Attaching preliminary CSVs and kernel profiles (quant_results_q2.csv, kernel_profiles_nodeA.zip). These are lab runs; not yet canary traffic. High-level summary below.

Summary (model X, sequence=512, batching tuned for latency targets):
- FP16 / BF16 baseline (node-A): p50 = 85 ms, p95 = 210 ms, TTFT = 40 ms, throughput = 780 tok/s at concurrency 16.
- INT8 (node-A, quantized with calibration): throughput +1.9x vs FP16 (≈1480 tok/s), p50 ~ 60 ms, but p95 increased to 260 ms, TTFT ~ 55 ms. Quality: exact-match delta = -1.5% (on our eval set).
- INT4 (experimental): throughput +2.7x, p50 ~ 48 ms, p95 ~ 410 ms, TTFT ~ 80 ms. Quality: exact-match delta = -4.8%, hallucination rate up ~2.3 pts.

Kernel profiling notes (node-A):
- Hotspot in GEMM kernel when sequence >384; one vendor kernel path shows 15-30% slower p95 vs alternative fused-attention kernel. We captured kernel traces in kernel_profiles_nodeA.zip.
- Preliminary patch (alt kernel selection + scheduling tweak) reduces p95 by ~18% in FP16 baseline in synthetic tests — will validate with real prompts.

Regression checks: we ran the eval harness (1200 prompt pairs) and computed the key metrics. Based on the acceptance criteria noted in MAP: INT8 is borderline but may be usable with route-level filtering and post-ranking. INT4 shows material quality regression and is not recommended for user-facing routes as-is.

Recommendations for MAP update:
1) Canary INT8 on non-critical routes first (demo/low-volume) with metrics collection and automatic rollback if exact-match drops >2% or p95 >250 ms for 10m sustained window.
2) Delay INT4 unless we can mitigate degradation via calibration + micro-LLM reranker; treat INT4 as experimental.
3) Apply kernel patch candidate to the canary pool and re-run baseline to recover p95 headroom before broad rollout.

Attachments: quant_results_q2.csv (CSV stub), kernel_profiles_nodeA.zip (tarball stub)

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: quant_results_q2.csv (CSV), kernel_profiles_nodeA.zip (zip)]

Date: 2026-04-17T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: MAP update & proposed close timeline (Canary start + acceptance criteria)

Sandra / team — based on Monica's results and your note on p95/TTFT priorities, I've updated the MAP actions and timeline. Key changes below; I will publish MAP_v1.1 and send the DocuSign link for the SLA once you ack.

Updated rollout plan (dates):
- Apr 20: Canary start (INT8) on demo + 5% of user traffic; enable kernel patch candidate on canary nodes
- Apr 20-29: Monitoring window (realtime dashboards + regression evals). Automated rollback triggers: exact-match delta <= -2% and/or p95 > 250 ms for >10m continuous period
- May 4: Planned broader rollout if canary passes

Owners & asks:
- Monica: execute kernel patch validation and run the regression harness on canary (owner: Monica)
- Vivek: prepare fallback routing policy and autoscaler thresholds for canary (owner: Vivek)
- Procurement / James: route DocuSign for SLA amendment by Apr 19 (owner: James)
- Sandra: confirm that Apr 30 is an acceptable 'close by' date for us to finalize commercial terms if canary passes earlier

Contingencies: If INT8 quality delta >2% during canary, we will: (a) pause canary; (b) roll back to FP16 for affected routes; (c) escalate to applied-ML for calibration adjustments.

Related links: hubspot deal (https://hubspot.example.com/deal/12345) + MAP doc in Drive.

Next steps: I will finalize MAP_EnterpriseAI_v1.1 (incorporating the rollback decision tree) and circulate DocuSign. Please reply with a quick ACK to proceed; if we get procurement sign-off by Apr 19 we can still meet the May 4 rollout target.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
